From 5c128a48829bd2caff4a061c5f4637d39c85ab6d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Johannes Schindelin <johannes.schindelin@gmx.de>
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2012 14:54:09 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] Updater: Brown paper bag fix

This fixes a bug. Basically, the bug would prevent any
shadowing (update sites overriding other update sites' files).

Signed-off-by: Johannes Schindelin <johannes.schindelin@gmx.de>

diff --git a/core/updater/core/src/main/java/imagej/updater/core/XMLFileReader.java b/core/updater/core/src/main/java/imagej/updater/core/XMLFileReader.java
index 316913918..bba523ecb 100644
--- a/core/updater/core/src/main/java/imagej/updater/core/XMLFileReader.java
+++ b/core/updater/core/src/main/java/imagej/updater/core/XMLFileReader.java
@@ -117,6 +117,7 @@ public void read(final String updateSite, final InputStream in,
 		SAXException
 	{
 		this.updateSite = updateSite;
+		filesFromThisSite.clear();
 		newTimestamp = timestamp;
 
 		final InputSource inputSource = new InputSource(in);
-- 
2.48.1

## Summary of Modifications

**File: `core/updater/core/src/main/java/imagej/updater/core/XMLFileReader.java`**

In the `read()` method, a single line was added: `filesFromThisSite.clear();`. This clears the `filesFromThisSite` collection at the start of each call to `read()`, before setting the `updateSite` field and processing the new update site's XML data.

**Relationship and Bug Explanation:**

The `XMLFileReader` class appears to be reused across multiple calls to `read()`, once for each update site being processed. The `filesFromThisSite` collection is likely used to track which files belong to the currently-processed update site, which in turn is used to determine file shadowing/override behavior (i.e., whether a file from one update site should override a file from another).

Without clearing this collection at the start of each `read()` call, stale data from a previous update site's processing would persist and accumulate across calls. This would corrupt the shadowing logic—since the collection would contain files from *multiple* update sites rather than just the current one—preventing the system from correctly determining that a file from a later-processed update site should override a file from an earlier one.

The fix ensures that `filesFromThisSite` only contains files relevant to the update site currently being read, restoring correct shadowing behavior between update sites.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
`public void read(final String updateSite, final InputStream in, final long timestamp) ... { this.updateSite = updateSite; newTimestamp = timestamp; ... }`
`filesFromThisSite` (instance field never cleared across calls)
Reason:
`read()` is called once per update site, but the instance field `filesFromThisSite` is never reset at the start of the method. As a result, entries from previously processed sites remain in the collection when parsing a new site's XML, causing it to accumulate files across all sites instead of holding only the current site's files. Since shadowing logic relies on `filesFromThisSite` to determine whether a file is new to the current site (and thus should override an earlier site's file), the stale accumulated data makes every file appear as if it already existed in the current site, so the override/shadowing logic never triggers correctly.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
`filesFromThisSite.clear();`
Reason:
By clearing `filesFromThisSite` at the very start of `read()`, the collection is guaranteed to contain only the files parsed from the update site currently being processed. This ensures the downstream shadowing check correctly identifies files that are new to the current site (and should override same-named files from previously processed sites), restoring correct shadowing behavior.

Root cause:
The `XMLFileReader.read()` method is invoked once per update site to parse that site's XML file list, and it uses the instance field `filesFromThisSite` to track which files belong to the site currently being processed. This collection was never reset between successive calls to `read()`, so when processing multiple update sites, `filesFromThisSite` accumulated entries from all previously processed sites rather than containing only the files belonging to the site currently being read. Since this collection is used downstream to determine shadowing logic (i.e., whether a file from the current update site should override a same-named file from a previously processed site), the stale, accumulated data caused the shadowing check to behave incorrectly—files that should have been recognized as newly introduced/overriding by the current site were instead treated as already present (from earlier sites), so shadowing/overriding never took effect correctly. Adding `filesFromThisSite.clear()` at the start of `read()` ensures the collection only reflects the current site's files, fixing the shadowing logic.
